### 1b. The seam is `AMGT-s-2`'s, not `AMGT-s-1`'s -- a plane note

PRD section 5 carries *"The desktop/cloud seam is crossed somehow"* as a precondition. Measured here:
`integrations/bloomberg/README.md` section 1 -- *"There is exactly one physical pipe, and it is loopback ...
DAPI binds 127.0.0.1 and nothing remote can reach it -- no VPN, peering, or security-group change. Something
running ON the Terminal box must make the blpapi call."* Section 5 lists **"Remote reach"** under what the
integration does NOT cover. The route inventory confirms no desktop origin exists.

⭐ **SO THE TWO BLOOMBERG CELLS SIT ON DIFFERENT SIDES OF THE SEAM, AND ONLY ONE NEEDS IT CROSSED.** A COVERED
name (`AMGT-s-1`) is served by the pattern the daily dashboard pull already runs in production: a job ON THE
BOX pulls, then publishes to S3, and the page reads the snapshot. Nothing crosses the seam inbound. An
UNCOVERED name typed into the page (`AMGT-s-2`) is a request that ORIGINATES in a browser served from AWS and
must reach the box -- that is the seam, and the estate has no precedent for it. **Hence `AMGT-s-2`'s first
deliverable is the design, not the build**, and `AMGT-s-1` is cut round 1 without waiting on it.

## 2. Four-postulate record (rule 24) for what this file ADOPTS and ADDS

Rule 24 binds any schema an agent authors **or ADOPTS**. This file adopts the PRD's manifest axes and the
sibling's cell-status vocabulary (2a); it adds the round axis (section 5) and the S4 split.

- **(i) MECE over a DECLARED domain.** Domain = the fourteen ratified outcomes `FWD-1`..`FWD-14`, reached
  through the fifteen manifest rows. Hunted in BOTH directions this file can hunt: **rows serving no cell:
  0 of 15; outcomes reached by no row: 0 of 14** (`FWD-10` is reached by S10 and S11, `FWD-3` by S3 and
  S11 -- the manifest's deliberate two-rows-one-outcome cases). **The S4 split is MECE over S4's own
  sources:** Seeking Alpha versus everything else, the boundary Andrew's hold draws, with no source in both
  cells and none in neither (IR channel, trusted publications -> `AMGT-s-4`; SA -> `AMGT-s-b4`).
- **(ii) SAME GRAIN.** Every cell is one ENGINE, the manifest's row grain. `AMGT-s-4` and `AMGT-s-b4` are two
  engines -- a reader and a fetch backend -- at the same grain as each other, not one nested in the other.
  `AMGT-s-2` and `AMGT-s-5` each carry two DELIVERABLES (a design, then a build) inside one engine; that is
  sequencing within a cell, not a second grain, and L6 cuts them as two criteria, never one compound one.
- **(iii) INTENT COHERENCE.** One axis per cell: what this engine must be able to answer. WHY a cell is
  bounded or held lives in section 2c and section 9, never as a cell state.
- **(iv) STATE COHERENCE -- which values one remedy does NOT move.** `AMGT-s-12` landing releases
  `AMGT-s-4`, `-8`, `-13`, `-15` (and the held `-b4`) from their root dependency; it does **not** move
  `AMGT-s-1`'s chain (`-2`, `-3`, `-5`, `-9`), `AMGT-s-6`'s (`-7`, `-14`) or `AMGT-s-11`'s (`-10`).
  **Andrew's release of the hold (@d09e26e1b1) MOVED `AMGT-s-b4` from HELD to OPEN and nothing else -- v0.2 of this file is the measurement: one row, one bounds line, the rounds, the holds.** The design-spec
  approval moves `AMGT-s-5`'s .tsx phase and nothing else. A repaired terminal sign-in moves the L6
  pre-spawn check on `AMGT-s-1`'s slot and no cell's state.
- **TOKEN CENSUS (word-boundary), owed with any value-enum proposal:** the only enum this file AUTHORS is the
  round axis (integers, section 5); the status vocabulary is adopted and its census is owed at L6 against the
  task-order and criteria corpus that does not exist yet, exactly as the sibling record states. **Recorded as
  a debt, not claimed.**

round's cells become cuttable early; the edges govern, the round numbers describe.

### 11c. Round-2 lessons absorbed into this cut

The round-2 cut carried three fixes that FAILED the CVO's judgment and two the CVO's own control caught.
This cut:

  two different numbers, so string-inequality proved nothing about the marker. Every round-2b difference
  arm holds the value FIXED and varies only the verdict / direction / check.

  (mechanically "a marker") that did not achieve at-a-glance salience (the judgment). rb-10's AC names the
  SALIENCE property (leading status, value not first), not merely "a marker field present".
- **Advertised contract == executed code.** r-15's docstring said AND, the code did OR. rb-15 makes the
  8-case truth table the acceptance and asserts the code matches the STATED contract.
- **A benefit claim states ONE denominator's category.** r-12's note mixed MEASURED and INFERRED under one
  "34 -> 49" number. rb-12 keeps the two categories separate with their own counts.
- **A source fix is not live until a CONSUMER reads it.** r-1 corrected the join on a new lane nothing
  consumes. rb-2 tests the consumer path; rb-1 + rb-2 is the pair that makes it served.
- Carried from round 1: every criterion DISCRIMINATES; the proof instance uses the FULL task-order stem
  filename; a criterion names the instrument that OBSERVES the artifact; the write grant is read while the
  order is NON-TERMINAL.

### 13e. Round-4 lessons absorbed into this cut

- **A cut may not rest on a gate's green when a row says the gate lies.** 13a is this lesson applied to the
  cut itself: the two-limb precondition exists because `Z-S6` measured a false green THIS ROUND, and
  `to-pipeline-gate` LIMB 6 reads the same false green, so it could not have been the backstop.
- **An id is minted from a RE-READ, never from recall.** Row `Z-S7` was minted by this lane from "S5 mine,
  S6 the CTO's, so S7 next" and collided with `4.0.0_SA_CRO~Z`'s committed `Z-S7`. Re-enumerating at write
  time gives the lowest free id; recall does not. The same applies to cell ids in this table.
- **An uncommitted channel row is an ESTATE-WIDE OUTAGE, not a personal todo** -- the standing-corpus pass
  reads the WORKTREE and is fail-closed, so it blocked a peer's unrelated drain. The window between
  appending a row and committing it is a shared-resource window.
- **An invented schema field is a violation even when it looks harmless** (`additionalProperties: false`
  rejects the KEY, and no value satisfies it). Rule 24 binds a schema ADOPTED as hard as one authored.
- Carried from prior rounds: every criterion DISCRIMINATES; the proof instance uses the FULL task-order stem
  filename; a criterion names the instrument that OBSERVES the artifact; an integration cell's `<paths>`
  names the CONSUMER's home.

### 13g. AMENDMENT v0.6.1 -- `/dispatch --plan` caught a WRONG EDGE and a wrong fan-out, BEFORE any order was issued

**This amendment is legal because NO ORDER IS ISSUED AND NO WORKER IS SPAWNED.** Rule 27's freeze binds
the decomposition MID-ROUND; between L5 and L6 with an empty `task-orders/` set for this round, a
correction is still an L5 act. Issuing against a knowingly-wrong edge would have been the worse choice.

**WHAT `--plan` MEASURED:** under the skill's own definition of M ("two cells joined by an edge are one
chain"), the v0.6 edge set formed **ONE connected component, not four chains** -- so the stated
`fanout: 2 of 4` was wrong, and taken literally it implied N = M = 1 and one worker serializing all eight
cells, which contradicts Andrew's "TABLES FIRST".

**THE CAUSE WAS A SUBSTANTIVE ERROR, NOT AN ARITHMETIC ONE.** v0.6 gave `rd-6` (the price axis) a
dependency on `rd-3` (the harvester box). That edge is WRONG on the constraint's own words:
`C-PRICE-RANKING-BOXSIDE` names the **ETF-daily-pull shape**, which runs on the **Bloomberg TERMINAL
box** against a loopback-only DAPI -- the same seam `AMGT-s-2` exists to cross. The NEW EC2 box of `rd-3`
hosts the four ARTICLE harvesters. Two different machines, two different concerns; the edge conflated
"box-side" with "the box this round builds". Removing it yields **M = 2**, which is what the two
independent roots were always going to be.
WARN: the wrong edge would ALSO have mis-scoped `rd-6`'s worker face -- it would have named the harvester
box's home in `<paths>` and omitted the terminal box's, and under RULING 1 a path missing from the order
is a WALL, not a hint. So this was on its way to a blocked worker, not just a wrong number.

**THE GENERAL FINDING, worth more than this instance:** rounds 1-4 were either INDEPENDENT cells (round 2:
5 of 5) or a single PATH (round 4: 1 of 1), and for both shapes "connected components" and "worker queues"
give the same number. **Round 5 is this project's first CONVERGENT DAG** -- two roots meeting at `rd-8` --
and it is the first shape where the two readings diverge. A fan-out number copied forward in the shape of
earlier rounds is exactly where that divergence hides.

2, fan-out corrected. Sections 1-12 unchanged and FROZEN.)*

## 44. ROUND 36 -- HKEXNEWS AS A RESEARCH QUESTION. One cell, and the finding that reshaped it before it was cut

**Cut by `2.0.0_SA_COO~Z`** on `1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z`'s ROUND-35 ANALYSIS @`401d59ce04` (msg 24721), with `AMGT_RESAPP`
v0.24 @`ddb93dd170` reading **ADMITTED** -- both halves SIGNED and current, **re-read at this cut, not inherited
from s.43.** LIMB 6 does not refuse a newly-added order.

The CTO's direction: *"A RESEARCH cell on HKEXnews's interface -- not a tuning pass (`Z-W128-S1`, unsoftened)."*
⭐ **That direction is correct and it is NOT SUFFICIENT, and 44a is why.**

### 44a. ⛔ THE HK ROUTE HAS **TWO** BLOCKERS, AND THE ONE WE MEASURED **MASKS** THE ONE WE DID NOT

Measured at HEAD before this order existed, `lib/research/filings/battery.py`:

| | blocker | how it was known |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | HKEXnews title search returns `recordCnt=0` | **REPORTED** -- round 35's AC4, the whole of `Z-W128-S1` |
| **B** | ⛔ **the adapter CANNOT WIN under ANY search result, and its `seeds` are UNREADABLE BY CONSTRUCTION** | ⛔ **NEVER REPORTED, by any of the three seats** |

**B, at the bytes:**

- `_hk_national_regulator` (`:1252-1334`) has **FIVE return paths and all five carry `"passed": False`** --
  including the branch where the search SUCCEEDS and populates `seeds` (`:1325-1334`).
- `seeds` is created at `:1441` and passed **BY REFERENCE into step 4's lambda** (`:1449`). **Step 4 is its only
  reader.**
- Step 5 runs at `:1451`, **AFTER step 4.** Its returned seeds merge at `:1460-1462` into that same list -- ⛔ **a
  list whose sole consumer has already executed. Step 5 writes its seeds into the past.**
- `winner_extra` is set only on `cached["passed"]` (`:1463`), never true here, so the run falls to `:1473` and
  `battery_block` is built from `attempts` alone (`:1476`). **`seeds` appears nowhere in the returned object.**

⭐ **THE DISCRIMINATOR, AND IT IS WHY THIS WAS INVISIBLE FROM ROUND 35's EVIDENCE: a round-36 cell that researched
the query and SUCCEEDED COMPLETELY would produce `recordCnt > 0`, a populated `seeds`, `passed` STILL FALSE, the
route STILL UNRESOLVED, and nothing downstream different.** The packet would read *"query solved, route still
unresolved"* and the next seat would hunt a THIRD cause that does not exist.

⛔ **AND B IS MINE, NOT THE WORKER'S.** It follows from the round-35 order's own egress bound -- ONE live HKEX
fetch, spent on the search -- which makes fetching the found document impossible, which makes `acceptance()`
unreachable, which makes `passed: True` unreachable. **The worker implemented that bound correctly and DOCUMENTED
IT EXACTLY**, at `:1267-1272`: *"this order's egress bound is ONE live HKEX fetch, already spent on the search ...
and no branch here ever wins."*

⚠ **So the sentence naming blocker B sat in the deliverable the whole time, in the worker's own docstring, and
three seats read that file without reading it.** Round 35's packet attributed the failure ENTIRELY to A. That was
not WRONG about A; it was **incomplete in the one direction that would have cost round 36.**

⭐ **THE CLASS, for the annex: when a route fails at the FIRST of two stacked blockers, the second is INVISIBLE TO
EVERY INSTRUMENT AIMED AT THE ROUTE, because the route never reaches it.** Only reading the code path PAST the
observed failure finds it. **Rule 22's shared-dependency blindness, rotated:** not a defect BENEATH the members,
but a defect DOWNSTREAM of the stop. COST: one read past the failure point. NON-APPLICATION: a route with a single
failure mode already proven exhaustive.

### 44b. THE MAPPING

| cell | id | serves | what it must answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| HKEXnews interface research + the win path | `AMGT-rk-129` | FWD-3 (Lenovo FILINGS -> Thesis tab); `rk-49`'s real dependency | whether HKEXnews can be made to return records AT ALL, and -- **independently** -- whether the adapter can WIN when it does |

### 44c. THE BOUNDS THAT ARE NOT NEGOTIABLE, and why each is here

1. ⛔ **A POSITIVE CONTROL COMES FIRST; THE CELL IS REFUSED WITHOUT ONE.** `recordCnt=0` today is
   **NON-DISCRIMINATING** -- it reads identically for wrong params, wrong endpoint, a required session/cookie, a
   silent block, and a genuine absence of filings. **Find ANY query to `titleSearchServlet.do` returning
   `recordCnt > 0`** -- any issuer, any range, the interface's own defaults. Until one exists, every conclusion
   about Lenovo is unfalsifiable. This is `Z-W128-S1`'s *"not a tuning pass"* made mechanical.
2. ⛔ **THE WIN PATH IS PROVEN AGAINST A FIXTURE, NEVER AGAINST THE LIVE SEARCH.** Limb 2 must be gradeable
   **whether or not limb 1 succeeds** -- a stubbed HKEXnews reply carrying one known-good record, exactly as round
   35 proved test (c) with a purpose-built synthetic `SC 13D`. ⭐ **This is the whole point of 44a: the two
   blockers are decoupled so neither can mask the other again.**
3. **Acceptance test (c) still BINDS** -- a document is accepted only if the issuer is the SUBJECT, not merely the
   filer. Round 35 proved it adversarially; widening the win path must not loosen it.
4. **Steps 1-4 do not move.** Signatures and call sites byte-identical, `STEP_ORDER` untouched, `_attempt`
   untouched -- negative-controlled by printing them before and after, as in round 35.
5. **Egress:** HKEX is a PUBLIC regulator interface, like EDGAR -- ⭐ **no vendor word needed** (`1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z`
   @`401d59ce04`, explicit). The bound rises from ONE fetch to a NAMED, PRINTED budget, **because the one-fetch
   bound is the direct cause of blocker B.** 0 Bloomberg calls.
6. ⛔ **STANDING, from the rk-128 cut forward: NO S3 DELETE OF ANY KIND** -- no object, no version, no delete
   marker (removing a delete marker is itself a delete). Andrew's word only.
7. ⛔ **STANDING: no hunting for a key, secret or session to forge a portal RS256 bearer.** If HKEXnews turns out
   to require a session, that is a **FINDING TO REPORT**, never a thing to manufacture.

### 44d. WHY BOTH LIMBS ARE ONE CELL AND NOT TWO ROUNDS

They are one cell because **cutting them apart re-creates the exact masking 44a just found.** A round shipping limb
1 alone ends at *"records now returned, route still unresolved"* -- which is where round 35 ended, one cause later.
A round shipping limb 2 alone cannot be graded live. ⭐ **Bound 2 is what makes one cell honest: limb 2 is
fixture-proven, so the cell delivers a gradeable result even if HKEXnews defeats limb 1 entirely.**

⚠ **AND THE HONEST STATEMENT OF WHAT THIS ROUND CAN DELIVER: if limb 1 finds HKEXnews genuinely unusable without
credentials, the route is CORRECTLY ABANDONED, and that is a FULL RESULT, not a failure** -- it retires a half-fix
that has now consumed parts of three rounds. **This cell is cut to be able to say NO.**

- **(i) MECE over a declared domain.** Domain = the ENDPOINT fence's `FWD-21`..`FWD-30` at `1ffb156ecd` (ten lines, read
  from the fence, not the addendum) **MINUS** nothing: all ten are cut. Written as a subtraction from the file's own count

  every surface cell renders; the `1ec5446c` deploy -> MSTR's act, not a cell; consumer-2, the failure cases and the
  `BP/_LN_Equity` route -> closer items under their own spec (B.5); **the overlay's point-read fallback is CARRIED, NOT CUT**
  (45g) -- it has no ratified mechanism text to cut a criterion from.
- **(ii) Same grain.** Every cell is a set of page-local source files plus the harness that renders them; no cell is a
  route, a payload or a shared component. The two wave-2 cells are the same grain (a script and a page-local module).

### 45d. THE BOUNDS THAT BIND EVERY CELL

1. **The contract is `portal/DESIGN.md` C1-C12** and a rejection cites a clause number (`C-CLAUSE-CITED-REJECTION`). The type
   ladder: body 16/400, numeral 14/400 tabular, label 13/700, footnote 11/400; nothing below 11px; weights 400 and 700
   only (C1); radii 2/3/4px or pill (C11); no `box-shadow` but the focus ring (C11); one band per page (C3); status as an
   icon beside navy text, never coloured text on a light ground (C6, C9); every empty panel one of the four designed
   states from `src/ui/components/states` (C12).
2. **THE VERIFICATION DIET.** Each build order carries at most three mechanical criteria: (a) the built behaviour proven by
   its own harness arm over the ACTUAL component through `react-dom/server`; (b) the class census over its owned files
   reading ZERO; (c) the shared harness it owns reading green. Repo-wide `tsc`, lint and the full harness set run at the
   drain, not on a face. The DOM instrument (`ui-contract-check.mjs`) is run by the issuer at every merge and by rl-1/rl-9.
3. **THE CLASS CENSUS (rl-1's third deliverable) IS THE MECHANICAL PROXY FOR C1/C5/C11 AT THE SOURCE**, printed per file
   with its denominator; the walk measured **246 idioms across 18 files** and the census reads that figure BEFORE any
   cell moves (positive control). Categories: light-on-dark and translucent idioms (`text-white*`, `bg-white/N`,
   `bg-black/N`, `text-<hue>-(100|200|300|400)`, any `<prefix>-<colour>-<n>/<opacity>`, `opacity-N`); sizes below 11
   (`text-[9px]`, `text-[10px]`, and any `text-[<n>px]` with n < 11); weights outside {400,700} (`font-light`, `font-medium`,
   `font-semibold`, `font-extrabold`, `font-black`, `font-thin`, `font-extralight`); radii outside {2,3,4,pill}
   (`rounded-md`, `rounded-lg`, `rounded-xl`, `rounded-2xl`, `rounded-3xl`, `rounded-[<n>px]` with n not in {2,3,4});
   shadows (`shadow`, `shadow-sm|md|lg|xl|2xl|inner`) not preceded by `focus-visible:`/`focus:`.
4. **NO CHANGE to `src/ui/**`, `src/components/**`, `src/api/**`, any route, any DTO, `package.json`, or the vite config.**
   A field a tile needs that the payload does not carry is RECORDED as a SERVED-RUNTIME ASK and the tile renders ABSENT
   with its reason (`C-PRESENTATION-ONLY`, the value-must-carry-its-claim law).
5. **NO INSTALL.** `node_modules` is linked by the provisioner. **No vite dev server on a wave-1 worker** (bound 2).
6. **Standing:** no S3 delete of any kind; no hunting for a key, secret or session; no vendor or Bloomberg call; no push,
   merge, rebase, `checkout --` or `clean`; no promote. `.scratch/**` has no lane -- scripts live under the worker's
   `deliverables/<serial>/` (grant-free), never `.scratch/`.
7. **What is KEPT (B.5, brief IV.9):** the verbatim gate and the PASS/REFUSE face, the three-state reads (SERVED / ABSENT /
   READ_FAILED never collapse), the generation caption's facts, the crossed-controls model, the Peers/Posture symmetry
   (`usePeerSet` for subject AND comparable), the "machine, never an instruction" marking. **The spec changes how these are
   shown, never whether.**

### 47b. THE P/E FINDING, SIZED AT THE CUT (item 3)

The CVO's Z-S265 says the reciprocal has no locatable implementation. **It has one:** `portal/src/pages/SecurityAnalysis/cscTable.ts:90-93`
computes `1 / value` for codes `ey` and `ey_ntm`. What is wrong is the UNIT the producer serves: the fixture the page renders
(`__harness__/tests/uiContractFixtures.json`, route `/api/scoped/amgt/security/BA_US_Equity/peers`) carries `ey` as a PERCENT
(DE 2.88, ETN 2.20, UNP 4.18; `factors.ey_ntm` 3.42, 3.32, 4.64), the peers package's own tests carry FRACTIONS (`ey` 0.02, -0.05;
`ey_ntm` 0.04), and the consumer's reciprocal assumes a fraction -- so 1/2.88 = 0.35 renders under "P/E (trailing)" where 34.7 is
the number (base run of `checks/rn-2.AC2.cjs`: 5 of 24 member values in [0.5, 200]). `csc.py:88-89` states the relation in PROSE
("RECIPROCAL: P/E = 1 / ey") and nothing machine-readable about units. The cell makes the producer STATE it (`transform`,
`units` on the map entry), makes the consumer apply it (100/x for percent, 1/x for fraction, null otherwise), patches the captured
fixtures' map entries to carry the fields, and carries the magnitude criterion the analysis owes (every member P/E in [0.5, 200] or
null). Which unit the LIVE producer serves is read by the cell from the registry and stated in its report.

### 98e. AMENDMENT 1 (issuer, 2026-10-11 ~06:0xZ) -- `AMGT-oo-4` is a BUILD cell, and it is ROUND 91's, not round 90's

The issuer's own record, corrected; no ENDPOINT or SERVED/WORLD change. s.98a, s.98b and s.98c named `AMGT-oo-4` an issuer read "DONE at
the cut, no build" on a count of 0 of 1,816 non-US rows resolved by the scanner's raw ticker. That count tested one form of the rule.
The live `_with_numeric_tickers` serves 29 of 769 all-digit non-US rows (22 by name, 7 by Japan code), and 23 of the other 1,047 name
exactly one held company and are not served (ISSUER_READS.md, CORRECTION; `reads/r90_measure_nonus3.py`). The CTO's item 2 therefore
has one buildable cell: the numeric rule's exact-name arm extended to non-digit tickers (ceiling 52 of 1,816; 1,764 keep their plain
reasons; no parser).

## 111. ROUND 103 -- THE OVERLAY'S FEED AND NEWS CARD READ ONLY THE SUBJECT'S ROWS (A BUILD, ITS STAGED APPLY AND THE DRIVEN COLD REQUEST); THE OVERLAY'S HANDLER TIME OVER A DECLARED WINDOW (A STAGED READ); THE ADMISSION TABLE'S ARMS; THE TOTAL-RETURN FIELD ON THE RESEARCH PRICE AXIS (SITE Z CODE). Two worker builds, one staged seat order, one staged read, one instrument.

**Issuer:** `2.0.0_SA_COO~R1` on dell1. **Input:** the CTO~DELL1 round-102 analysis `ledger/ROUND_ANALYSIS.round102.md` @2c3cf03abb (msg 4958) section 2, after the CVO's slug (msg 4954,
`ADJUDICATION_v124` @4a8f8b49eb, MAY-CLOSE). **Prefix:** `bj` (round 103). Round 102 attributed the cold overlay (the first overlay a container serves is about 20 s; 91 percent of it is `feed`, inside it
the whole-table gold read) and applied the phase log lines (`bKCGUhXp..`, 2026-10-13T16:15:54Z).

### 111a. MEASURED AT THE CUT

- **The remedy already exists in the module.** `_timeline_snapshot_rows(table, columns=..., security_key=...)` (`scoped_amgt.py`, AMGT-an-5) reads ONE security's rows of ONLY the named columns; the
  timeline route uses it. The overlay's two readers of `article_security_mention` (`read_feed`, `_overlay_top_band`) call it with neither, so the table is decoded whole and turned into Python
  rows for all securities. The prototype (blob 84002d3fd559, +9 -2: one column tuple, two call sites) serves overlay bytes EQUAL to the base for ASML_NA, four drawn covered keys and a
  covered key with no mention rows (16 of 16 arms), and leaves no whole-snapshot cache entry.
- **What the prototype does NOT prove.** Locally the snapshot (8.4 MB object, 52,424 rows, 31 columns) costs list 0.23 s, GET 0.38 s, full decode 0.30 s, `to_pylist` 0.78 s; the projected decode
  is 0.01 s and the key column 0.003 s. Lambda ran the whole-table phase 12 times slower than the box. The key-scoped path still LISTs and GETs the object once per container; whether feed
  reaches the CTO's 2 s on Lambda is read at the driven request (`bj-2`), not claimed. A second whole-table reader exists (`_overlay_top_band`): fixing only `read_feed` would have moved the
  18 s to the news card, which is why ONE tuple serves both.

### 117c. ADDENDUM 3 -- THE CUT OF `AMGT-bo-7` (G4: THE TRIGGER'S EVENT READS THE SAME KEY LIST), 2026-10-16 ~12:1xZ

Found by the issuer while writing the COO half for the 8-key re-enable: `filings/batch.py` uses `plan_only_check` (the skip-on-unchanged read) ONLY under `--plan-only`; a real run (`run_group`) re-fetches and re-analyzes every name in its plan every time. The trigger's event for the filings task is the UNFILTERED `--plan-only` WOULD-RUN count (171 on 2026-10-16, 163 of them names whose expected form is `none` and can never resolve), so it stays above zero forever: a task enabled with the 8-key list would re-analyze those 8 EVERY trading day (about USD 4.5 to 5.6 a day), not once. My earlier statements that a second day's run "skips them as unchanged" were wrong for the real run. `AMGT-bo-7` (slot `~481`, workstream `G4PLAN`, risk LOCAL, write surface `lib/research/llm_batch/`) makes `would_run` and `run_task` pass the same key list to the plan-only command, so the event counts only those 8: after one good run all 8 read SKIP-UNCHANGED, the count is 0 and the task is not due. It lands before the re-enable. Not in this cell: the whole-universe event definition (`none`-form names are counted as would-run forever), a question for the CTO. fanout: 1 of 1 chains, cap 8, reason: bo-7 follows bo-5 (it edits the files bo-5 changed, now merged) and runs beside `bo-6` (the filings batch, a different module).

**Decisions this decomposition takes (the issuer's, inside the CTO's reading).** (a) A list of records in a changed figure's `from` or `to` prints its NEWEST entry (the served list is newest first) as `<announcement_date> (<period>)` for an earnings-dates figure and as `<n> entries` for any other list; no served value moves. (b) The CTO's "the label comes from the period's real name" meets a data fact: the stored segment source carries no period name, only the reconciliation of column sums to reported revenue (`segment_period.label_periods`) names a column; for RIO LN's column 5 (sum 106861, no year ties) there is no real name to read. The cell tests whether any stored value names it; if none does, it neither guesses a year nor keeps the vendor's `Period 5`: it labels the column in words as a column whose year is not stated. (c) A money tile prints `$` only when its currency is the name's price currency and that is USD; a tile in any other currency prints its ISO code first (`USD 33.11B` beside PHP tiles, `PHP 860.00`), and the sign leads the whole figure (`-$63.90B`, `-PHP 3.65B`). (d) `AMGT-bp-2` reads CTO item 1's "on a local build of PROD first" as PROD plus the fix: the unpatched PROD build is the known crash.
